West as Treasurer, and adopted the annual resolutions on fund depositories, legal counsel, meeting schedule and committee assignments. **Meeting**
Troy Board of Education organizational and regular meeting, January 17, 2023, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; adjournment at 8:21 p.m. Present: Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, Schmidt and Wilson; Superintendent Machesky; administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris and West; four high school student representatives and approximately 25 members of the audience. Minutes signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

**Organizational actions (23-001 through 23-011)**
Mr. Schmidt was named acting chairperson (23-001) and appointed Judy Holmes temporary secretary. Dr. Wilson nominated Mr. Schmidt for president; Mr. Hauff nominated Dr. Wilson for vice president; Mrs. Anne nominated Mr. Hauff for secretary. Each officer was elected by roll call, 7 yes to 0 no, to serve until December 31, 2023 (23-002, 23-003, 23-004). Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, was appointed Treasurer for January through December 2023 (23-005). The Board adopted the Fund Depositories and Investments resolution (23-006) naming Bank of America, Citizens Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Huntington Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank) and PNC Bank; investments follow Board Policy 5000.06 and Section 380.1223(1)(h) of the Revised School Code. Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Miller Johnson; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Miller Canfield were continued as legal counsel for the 2023 calendar year (23-007). The Superintendent was continued as Deputy Secretary (23-008), Judy Holmes designated to post meeting notices (23-009), and the 2023 meeting schedule (23-010) and Board committee memberships (23-011) adopted, each 7-0.

**Recognitions**
The Superintendent Student Advisory Board Executive Committee, which leads the 60-member SSAB and organized the District's MLK Celebration and Day of Service attended by over 800 people, was recognized: Aanvi Arora, Allison Diebol, George Perakis, Akshitha Sahu, Aanya Shah, Marlien William and Ray Zhang. The Student Spotlight featured Troy High School sophomore Akshaya Rachamadugu for her directorial debut short film, introduced by Thomas Butcher. January was observed as School Board Appreciation Month.

**Consent agenda (23-012)**
Approved 7-0: December 6, 2022 Workshop minutes; December 13, 2022 Board Meeting minutes; Treasurer's Report – November 2022; and the Stormwater Management Program.

**Business awards**

| Item | Award | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| BP 9951 turf/track (23-013) | S&H Trucking & Excavating, LLC (Alt A) site work, turf | $483,000.00 |
| | Shaw Integrated & Turf Solutions, Inc (Alt E) synthetic turf | $580,458.00 |
| | Goddard Coatings (Alt G) track surface | $144,105.00 |
| | Nagle Paving, site work, track | $534,790.00 |
| | Contingency | $87,117.00 |
| | Total, Building Site & Sinking Fund and/or 2023 Bond Fund | $1,829,470.00 |
| BP 9954 THS gym bleachers (23-014) | Interkal, LLC | $490,396.20 |
| BP 955 flooring (23-015) | Conventional Carpet, Inc., flooring demo/replacement | $1,223,713.00 |
| | Paint Plus LLC, floor polishing | $70,493.00 |
| | Additional/Emergency Flooring | $30,000.00 |
| | Total | $1,324,206.00 |
| Cafeteria tables, Troy Union and Hamilton (23-016) | School Specialty, Community Service Fund | $89,629.12 |

**Public comment and announcements**
Janice Girling addressed labeling of parents who voice concerns; Ollie Apahidean addressed media center materials. Mr. Schmidt announced an outside security company consulting on District safety procedures, a February 7 workshop and a February 14 Board meeting.
2023_074_m011723org_regbdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the Troy Board of Education organizational and regular meeting held Tuesday, January 17, 2023 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris and West. Four high school student representatives and approximately 25 members of the audience attended. Mr. Schmidt explained that this meeting is where the Board elects officers, appoints committee members for the upcoming year, and approves items considered on an annual basis, with the regular Board meeting to follow. The minutes were submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (GNH/jh).

ELECTION OF ACTING CHAIRPERSON (23-001): Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Dr. Wilson, that Mr. Schmidt serve as acting chairperson to officiate until the election of a president was completed. Yes: 7, No: 0. Mr. Schmidt then appointed Judy Holmes to act as temporary secretary until the secretary of the Troy Board of Education was elected.

NOMINATION AND ELECTION OF PRESIDENT (23-002): Acting Chairperson Schmidt declared nominations in order; Dr. Wilson nominated Mr. Schmidt. Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Dr. Wilson, that nominations be closed; Yes: 7, No: 0. Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Dr. Wilson, that Mr. Schmidt serve as president of the Troy Board of Education until December 31, 2023. Roll call vote of Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, Schmidt and Wilson, all yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

NOMINATION AND ELECTION OF VICE PRESIDENT (23-003): Mr. Hauff nominated Dr. Wilson. Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Dr. Philippart, that nominations be closed; Yes: 7, No: 0. Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Dr. Philippart, that Dr. Wilson serve as vice president until December 31, 2023. Roll call, all yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

NOMINATION AND ELECTION OF SECRETARY (23-004): Mrs. Anne nominated Mr. Hauff. Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Dr. Wilson, that nominations be closed (the minutes as printed refer to nominations for vice president in this motion); Yes: 7, No: 0. Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mrs. Anne, that Mr. Hauff serve as secretary until December 31, 2023. Roll call, all yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

APPOINTMENT OF SCHOOL BOARD TREASURER (23-005): Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Dr. Wilson, that Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, be appointed Treasurer of the Troy Board of Education for the period January through December 2023. Yes: 7, No: 0.

ESTABLISH FUND DEPOSITORIES AND INVESTMENTS (23-006): Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mr. Haupt, adopting the resolution for January through December 2023, with the attached resolution incorporated in full into the official minutes. The resolution recites that Michigan law requires the Board to provide by resolution for deposit of all public monies, including tax monies, coming into the hands of Rick West, Treasurer of Troy School District. Designated depository institutions: Bank of America, Citizens Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Huntington Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), and PNC Bank. Monies may be withdrawn by checks bearing the facsimile signature of Treasurer Rick West, and in emergencies the handwritten signature of Rick West or Superintendent Richard M. Machesky, who may sign on the General Fund account and the Payroll account at Bank of America. Accounts established at PNC Bank for paying Troy Career Center expenses may be drawn on by handwritten signature of the Troy Career Center Manager, Assistant Manager, or Program Coordinators. The Treasurer may open or close accounts with the listed institutions when in the District's interest; District funds may be invested according to Board Policy 5000.06; and the Treasurer may combine money from more than one fund for an investment authorized by subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. The maximum amount to be invested is regulated by the school code. Gary Hauff, Secretary of Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, certified adoption of the resolution under hand and seal this 17th day of January 2023. Yes: 7, No: 0.

DESIGNATION OF BOARD AND DISTRICT LEGAL COUNSEL (23-007): Moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mrs. Alic, to continue the designation of Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Miller Johnson; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Miller Canfield as legal counsel to advise and/or represent the Troy School District and Board of Education for the 2023 calendar year, with the superintendent authorized to consult additional counsel as needed with prior notification to the board. Yes: 7, No: 0.

DESIGNATION OF SUPERINTENDENT AS DEPUTY SECRETARY (23-008): Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mr. Hauff, continuing the Superintendent of Schools as Deputy Secretary of the Board with authority to act for the secretary for the 2023 calendar year. Yes: 7, No: 0.

DESIGNATION OF PERSON FOR POSTING NOTICES OF MEETINGS (23-009): Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mr. Hauff, designating Judy Holmes, Secretary to the Superintendent of Schools, for the 2023 calendar year. Yes: 7, No: 0.

MEETING SCHEDULE (23-010): Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mrs. Anne, adopting the schedule of meetings for the 2023 calendar year per the attached calendar. Yes: 7, No: 0. COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS (23-011): Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mr. Haupt, adopting the Board Committee Memberships for the 2023 school year as attached. Yes: 7, No: 0.

RECOGNITION: The TSD Mission Moment honored the Superintendent Student Advisory Board Executive Committee, which leads the 60 members of the SSAB by planning and running meetings and setting agendas; it was the first year the group had an executive board. The committee organized and executed the District's MLK Celebration and Day of Service, attended by over 800 people, requiring hundreds of hours of planning, soliciting thousands of dollars in donations and supplies, and organizing volunteers with minimal staff support; a video by a Troy Schools Creative Guild student showed highlights. Recognized with a token of appreciation: Aanvi Arora, Allison Diebol, George Perakis, Akshitha Sahu, Aanya Shah, Marlien William and Ray Zhang. The Student Spotlight featured Troy High School sophomore Akshaya Rachamadugu, who wrapped up editing on her first directorial debut short film; Thomas Butcher showed a clip, and she answered Board questions and received a certificate of recognition. January is School Board Appreciation Month; Dr. Machesky thanked the trustees and presented each with a gift.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS: None. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (non-agenda items), first period: None.

REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES: Mr. Schmidt invited the student representatives to report before continuing, as they needed to prepare for mid-terms. Yara Mashal (International Academy-East), Nish Palepu (Troy High School), Sara Ali (Athens High School) and Sophia Lelli, filling in for Alexi Papadelis (Troy College and Career High School), each reported on events and activities in their schools.

CONSENT AGENDA (23-012): Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mrs. Alic, approving items A, B, C and D: minutes of the December 6, 2022 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the December 13, 2022 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report – November 2022; and the Stormwater Management Program. Yes: 7, No: 0. Personnel: none. Curriculum: none.

BUSINESS. BP 9951 – 2023 THS Turf Replacement and BPMS Track Replacement (23-013): Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Dr. Wilson, awarding the bid and approving $1,829,470.00 as an expenditure of the Building Site & Sinking Fund and/or the 2023 Bond Fund: Site Work (turf), S&H Trucking & Excavating, LLC (Alt A), $483,000.00; Synthetic Turf, Shaw Integrated & Turf Solutions, Inc (Alt E), $580,458.00; Track Surface, Goddard Coatings (Alt G), $144,105.00; Site Work (track), Nagle Paving, $534,790.00; Contingency, $87,117.00; TOTAL $1,829,470.00. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BP 9954 – THS Gym Bleachers Replacement Project (23-014): Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mrs. Alic, awarding bleacher replacement to Interkal, LLC in the amount of $490,396.20 as an expenditure of the Building Site & Sinking Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BP 955 – 2023 Flooring Replacement and Polishing Project (23-015): Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Dr. Philippart, awarding flooring replacement work as an expenditure of the Building Site & Sinking Fund and Community Service Fund: Conventional Carpet, Inc., flooring demo/replacement, $1,223,713.00; Paint Plus LLC, floor polishing, $70,493.00; Additional/Emergency Flooring, $30,000.00; TOTAL $1,324,206.00. Yes: 7, No: 0.

Cafeteria Tables – Troy Union and Hamilton (23-016): Moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mr. Hauff, awarding the purchase of cafeteria tables to School Specialty in the amount of $89,629.12 as an expenditure of the Community Service Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (non-agenda items), second period: Ms. Janice Girling, Troy resident and parent of a junior at Athens High School, addressed the Board about labeling and targeting parents who voice their concerns and mentioned an article in the Troy High School newspaper. Mr. Ollie Apahidean, Troy resident and parent of students in the district, spoke about materials and books available in the school media centers and pornography. Other: none.

BOARD COMMENTS: Dr. Philippart welcomed the two new board members and thanked the officers serving another year; Mr. Haupt thanked everyone for the warm welcome; Mrs. Anne thanked the current officers and noted she attended the IAE Culture Show; Mrs. Alic said she was excited to work with the group; Mr. Hauff thanked everyone for their confidence. Dr. Wilson welcomed the new board members, thanked the community for supporting the MLK Day event, and announced Troy High Activist Week and Athens Charity Week. Dr. Machesky announced the Festival of Choirs Monday through Thursday at Athens, meetings set with newly elected legislators on the district's legislative priorities, and several board members attending the Advocacy Institute in Washington, DC. Mr. Schmidt described the MLK Day event as inspiring, noted an outside security company is consulting with the District to review all safety and security procedures in detail, and announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, February 7th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building and the next Board Meeting for Tuesday, February 14th at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building.

ADJOURNMENT: The meeting was adjourned at 8:21 p.m.
